examples.ko: 큰 공을 세운 장군이 결국 토사구팽을 당했어요.
examples.en: The general who had done great service ended up being discarded.
It is too much that he, who built up the company, was cast aside.
Using someone and then throwing them away is like killing the hunting dog once the hunt is over.
Criticism emerged that they cast him aside right after the election.
I worked hard, but I am afraid of being used and then dropped.
I learned the idiom about killing the hound after the hunt in history class.

explain: 필요할 때는 쓰다가 쓸모가 없어지면 버린다는 비판의 느낌으로 써요. 뉴스에서 정치나 회사 인사 이야기에 자주 나오고, '토사구팽당하다'라는 말을 많이 써요. 가까운 사이의 일상 대화보다는 글이나 토론에서 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It carries a critical tone, about someone being used when needed and dropped once no longer useful. It often appears in news about politics or company personnel matters, commonly as '토사구팽당하다'. It sounds more natural in writing or debate than in casual chat between close friends.

examples.en: The independence activists fought without fearing imprisonment.

examples.ko: 그 작가는 투옥 중에도 글쓰기를 멈추지 않았어요.
examples.en: That writer didn't stop writing even while in prison.
As his imprisonment dragged on, his family had a very hard time.
A protest was held against the unjust imprisonment.

examples.ko: 오랜 투옥은 한 사람에게 큰 고통이에요.
examples.en: Long imprisonment is great suffering for a person.

examples.ko: 긴 투옥 끝에 그는 자유의 몸이 되었어요.
examples.en: After a long imprisonment, he became a free man.

explain: 사람을 감옥에 가두는 일을 가리켜서 역사 이야기나 뉴스에서 주로 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '감옥에 가다'라고 하고, 글에서는 '투옥되다'나 '투옥하다' 형태로도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to putting a person in prison and mostly appears in historical accounts and news. In daily talk people say '감옥에 가다', and in writing it often appears as '투옥되다' or '투옥하다'.

examples.en: This match was ruled a draw.

examples.ko: 검사 결과 아무 문제가 없다고 판정돼요.
examples.en: The test result is judged to show no problem.

examples.ko: 그 공이 아웃으로 판정되면 점수가 안 나요.
examples.en: If that ball is ruled out, no point is scored.

examples.ko: 심사 끝에 이 그림은 일등으로 판정되었어요.
examples.en: After the judging, this painting was ruled first place.

examples.ko: 불량으로 판정된 제품은 팔 수 없어요.
examples.en: Products judged to be defective cannot be sold.
I'm curious how the result will be decided.

explain: '판정되다'는 심판, 심사위원, 의사가 내린 결정으로 결과가 정해질 때 써요. 주어는 사람이 아니라 경기, 공, 제품, 검사 결과예요. 결정을 내리는 쪽은 '판정하다'이고, '판정을 내리다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: 판정되다 is used when a referee, a judging panel, or a doctor's decision settles a result. The subject is not a person but things like a match, a ball, a product, or test results. The one making the decision uses 판정하다, or the phrase '판정을 내리다'.

examples.en: I received a certificate of commendation at school for volunteer work.

examples.ko: 아버지는 오랜 근무로 회사에서 표창장을 받으셨어요.
examples.en: My father received a commendation from his company for his long service.
The teacher gave a certificate of commendation to the class representative.

examples.ko: 표창장은 액자에 넣어서 거실에 걸어 두었어요.
examples.en: I put the commendation certificate in a frame and hung it in the living room.

examples.ko: 표창장에 이름이 잘못 적혀 있어서 다시 받았어요.
examples.en: My name was written wrong on the certificate, so I got a new one.
The mayor presented certificates of commendation to the firefighters.

explain: '상장'은 시험이나 대회에서 잘한 사람이 받고, '표창장'은 봉사, 모범 행동, 오랜 공로처럼 칭찬할 일을 한 사람에게 줘요. '표창장을 받다/주다'로 쓰고, 상을 주는 일은 '표창하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: A '상장' goes to someone who did well in an exam or contest, while a '표창장' is given to someone praised for volunteering, model behavior or long service. It is used as '표창장을 받다' or '주다', and the act of awarding is '표창하다'.

examples.en: The people demanded the president's resignation.

examples.ko: 하야 소식에 뉴스가 하루 종일 떠들썩했어요.
examples.en: The news was buzzing all day over the resignation.
Protesters are shouting for the minister to step down.

examples.ko: 그는 하야 후 조용히 고향에서 지냈어요.
examples.en: After stepping down, he lived quietly in his hometown.

examples.ko: 총리의 하야 발표 이후 정치권이 바빠졌어요.
examples.en: After the prime minister announced his resignation, the political world got busy.

examples.ko: 하야 요구가 거세지자 그는 결국 물러났어요.
examples.en: As the calls to step down grew stronger, he finally left office.

explain: 대통령이나 총리처럼 높은 자리에 있는 사람이 물러날 때 뉴스에서 써요. 회사에서 그만둘 때는 '퇴사'나 '사직'이라고 해서 '하야'는 어울리지 않아요. '하야를 요구하다', '하야를 발표하다'처럼 같이 쓰는 말이 거의 정해져 있어요.
explain_en: News uses it when someone in a top post, such as a president or prime minister, leaves office. For quitting a company you would say '퇴사' or '사직', so '하야' does not fit. It is mostly used in set phrases like '하야를 요구하다' and '하야를 발표하다'.

examples.ko: 적의 공격으로 성이 사흘 만에 함락됐어요.
examples.en: The castle fell in three days under the enemy's attack.

examples.ko: 수도가 함락되자 많은 사람이 피난을 떠났어요.
examples.en: When the capital fell, many people left to take refuge.
If the fortress falls, the whole country is in danger.
There was a scene in the drama where the castle falls.

examples.ko: 요새가 함락될 거라고 아무도 생각하지 못했어요.
examples.en: Nobody thought the fortress would fall.

examples.ko: 도시가 함락된 뒤에도 사람들은 끝까지 버텼어요.
examples.en: Even after the city fell, the people held out to the end.

explain: 성, 도시, 요새처럼 지키던 곳이 공격을 받아 적에게 넘어갈 때 써요. '성이 함락되다', '수도가 함락되다'처럼 말하고, 반대로 끝까지 막아 낼 때는 '지키다'나 '방어하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used when a defended place such as a castle, city or fortress falls to an attack. People say '성이 함락되다' or '수도가 함락되다', and for the opposite, holding out to the end, they use '지키다' or '방어하다'.

examples.en: The person who went hiking has been missing for three days.
My wallet has been missing since yesterday.
We heard the news that the missing child was found.
My grandfather went missing during the war.
Two sailors were listed as missing.
I went to the police station to report a missing person.

explain: 사람이 어디 있는지 알 수 없을 때 써요. 물건이 안 보이면 '잃어버렸다', '없어졌다'를 쓰고, 농담으로 지갑이 행방불명이라고도 해요. '실종'은 사고 느낌의 뉴스 말이고, '행방불명'은 어디로 갔는지 모른다는 점이 중심이에요.
explain_en: Use it when nobody knows where a person is. For lost objects people say 잃어버렸다 or 없어졌다, but jokingly say a wallet is 행방불명. 실종 is a news word with an accident feel, while 행방불명 focuses on not knowing where someone went.

examples.en: Modernizing the factory cost a lot of money.
The market modernization project will end soon.
Modernizing the hospital facilities is urgent.
Thanks to agricultural modernization, farming has become much easier.

examples.ko: 도시가 현대화되면서 옛 건물이 많이 사라졌어요.
examples.en: As the city modernized, many old buildings disappeared.
The hanok was modernized and turned into a cafe.

explain: 낡은 시설이나 제도를 새롭게 바꾼다는 뜻으로 '시설 현대화', '시장 현대화'처럼 자주 써요. '근대화'는 역사 이야기에서 더 많이 나와요. 동사로는 '현대화하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is often used in phrases like '시설 현대화' and '시장 현대화' for updating old facilities or systems. '근대화' appears more in historical contexts. The verb form is '현대화하다'.

examples.en: That village became a victim of the war.

examples.ko: 어른들 싸움에 아이들을 희생물로 삼으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't make children the victims of adults' fights.
He was a victim of a false rumor.

examples.ko: 유행의 희생물이 되지 않으려면 스스로 판단해야 해요.
examples.en: To avoid becoming a victim of trends, you have to judge for yourself.
When the company ran into trouble, he was pushed out like a scapegoat.

examples.ko: 개발의 희생물인 오래된 골목을 지키자는 이야기가 나왔어요.
examples.en: People started talking about protecting the old alley that fell victim to development.

explain: '~의 희생물이 되다'처럼 어떤 힘이나 상황 때문에 피해를 보는 사람이나 것에 써요. 비슷한 '희생양'은 남의 잘못을 대신 떠안는 느낌이 더 강해요. '희생자'는 사람에게만 쓰는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: It is used in '~의 희생물이 되다' for a person or thing that suffers because of some force or situation. The similar '희생양' stresses taking the blame for others more strongly. '희생자', by contrast, refers only to people.
